name: Ur's Third Dynasty
summary: Sumer's last great age, when the kings of Ur ruled southern Mesopotamia and built its great ziggurat: the world Abram's family left.
dateNote: About 2112–2004 BC. On the early dating Abram leaves Ur near its end; on the late dating, after its fall, under the Old Babylonian kings.

name: Egypt's Middle Kingdom
summary: Egypt reunited under strong pharaohs, wealthy and settled, trading with Canaan: on the early dating, the Egypt Abram visits and Joseph rules.
dateNote: About 2055–1650 BC (the 11th to 13th dynasties). Egyptian dates this early can be off by a few decades.

name: The Old Babylonian kingdom
summary: Babylon rises to rule Mesopotamia, most famously under Hammurabi and his laws, until the Hittites sack the city.
dateNote: About 1894–1595 BC, in the middle chronology most historians use.

name: The Hyksos in Egypt
summary: Rulers from Canaan and Syria, "foreign kings" to the Egyptians, govern the Nile Delta from Avaris. Late-daters place Joseph and Jacob's family here.
dateNote: About 1650–1550 BC (the 15th dynasty). Avaris lay beside the later city of Rameses.

name: The Hittite Empire
summary: A great power of Anatolia that rivalled Egypt for Syria, until it collapsed with the end of the Bronze Age. Scripture's Hittites in Canaan (Ephron, Uriah) are a related people.
dateNote: About 1650–1180 BC, ruled from Hattusa in central Turkey.

name: Egypt's New Kingdom
summary: Egypt at its height, ruling Canaan through vassal kings. Its pharaohs include Thutmose III and Amenhotep II, the early-date candidates for the Exodus, and Ramesses II, the late-date one.

name: Egypt divided
summary: Egypt split between rival dynasties, Libyan and then Kushite, and no longer a power in Canaan except in raids like Shishak's, and as an ally Israel and Judah hoped in.
dateNote: About 1070–664 BC, Egypt's Third Intermediate Period. Shishak (Shoshenq I) and Tirhakah are its pharaohs in Scripture.

name: The Assyrian Empire
summary: The first great empire of the iron age, feared for its cruelty. It takes Samaria and scatters the northern tribes, and besieges Jerusalem under Hezekiah.
dateNote: The Neo-Assyrian Empire, 911–609 BC: Nineveh fell in 612, and its last king's stand at Haran in 609.

name: Egypt's Late Period
summary: Egypt revives under the Saite pharaohs, Neco among them, then falls to Persia. Jeremiah warns Judah not to trust it.
dateNote: 664–332 BC, including two spells of Persian rule (525–404 and 343–332 BC), until Alexander took Egypt.

name: The Babylonian Empire
summary: Nebuchadnezzar's empire, which destroys Jerusalem and its temple and carries Judah into exile.
dateNote: The Neo-Babylonian Empire, from Nabopolassar in 626 BC until Cyrus took Babylon in 539.

name: The Persian Empire
summary: The largest empire yet, from India to Egypt. Its kings let the exiles go home and rebuild the temple, and Esther is its queen.
dateNote: The Achaemenid Empire, from Cyrus's rise about 550 BC until Alexander defeated Darius III in 330.

name: Alexander's empire
summary: In a dozen years Alexander of Macedon conquers the Persian Empire and spreads Greek language and culture across the east; at his death his generals divide it.

name: The Seleucid Empire
summary: The Greek kingdom of Syria, founded by one of Alexander's generals. It takes Judea from the Ptolemies in 200 BC; its king Antiochus IV outlaws Judaism, sparking the Maccabean revolt.
dateNote: 312–63 BC, when Pompey made Syria a Roman province.

name: The Ptolemaic kingdom
summary: The Greek kingdom of Egypt, ruled from Alexandria by Alexander's general Ptolemy and his heirs. It rules Judea for a century, and its Jews translate the Septuagint.
dateNote: 305–30 BC, ending with Cleopatra. It ruled Judea from about 301 to 200 BC.

name: The Hasmonean kingdom
summary: The Maccabees' heirs rule an independent Jewish state as high priests and then kings, until civil war brings in Rome.
dateNote: From 140 BC, when Simon was made ruler, until Herod took Jerusalem in 37 BC; under Rome's rule from 63 BC.

name: The Roman Republic
summary: Rome governed by its senate and elected consuls, growing from a city on the Tiber to master of the Mediterranean. Its general Pompey takes Jerusalem.
dateNote: Traditionally from 509 BC, when Rome expelled its last king, until Augustus became emperor in 27 BC.

name: The Roman Empire
summary: Rome under its emperors: the world of the New Testament, whose roads and peace carry the gospel, and whose governors try Jesus and Paul.
dateNote: From Augustus in 27 BC. The western empire ended in AD 476; the eastern lasted until 1453.
